title: Saffron Finance - POC scoping: workload & traffic modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization for a retrieval-augmented chat assistant. Discussed QPS/concurrency targets, input/output token distributions, benchmarking plan (latency and cost), and 6-week pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run sample benchmark on customer anonymized traces, send proposed test plan and pricing, schedule deep-dive on VPC onboarding.
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark test plan and pricing sheet by 2027-03-14
Saffron: provide anonymized request traces and token histograms by 2027-03-16
Schedule VPC onboarding deep-dive with infra team (Carlos + Liam) week of 2027-03-21
action_items: Jamie Lin: Send POC test plan + pricing (due: 2027-03-14)
Maya Patel: Export 7 days of anonymized request logs & token histograms (due: 2027-03-16)
Carlos Vega: Prepare VPC checklist and sample terraform snippets (due: 2027-03-18)
transcript:
00:00 Jamie Lin: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll just give a quick agenda 
 scope the poc, get the workload numbers, success criteria and timelines, sound good?
00:08 Maya Patel: yeah sounds good. sorry i'm on a bit of a delay today, connection is meh but should be fine
00:15 Carlos Vega: quick intro, im carlos se, i'll own the benchmark and vpc bits, jamie is your ae on the account

00:25 Sophia Zhang: thanks, we want to validate cost and latency for our RAG chat assistant. primary constraint is sub-200ms p95 for short queries and throughput of about 30 qps during peak, with bursts to 120 qps for 30s windows

00:40 Liam O'Connor: to add, our concurrency is mostly user-driven 
 web chat sessions, about 3k concurrent sessions but active QPS is lower, typical concurrency to model is 70-120 concurrent requests at peak
01:05 Jamie Lin: ok good, can you confirm input token distribution? we typically model tail latencies differently for long context vs short prompts

01:15 Maya Patel: yes the modal input length is around 80 tokens, median 64, 95th at 420. Output is usually 40-120 tokens, modal 60. i'll share histograms. we've got a heavy tail from some long transcripts
01:40 Carlos Vega: good, that helps a lot. for benchmarks we'll run with samples at median, 75th, and 95th percentiles. we'll also test with kv cache warm and cold to see p95 impact

02:10 Sophia Zhang: are you suggesting dedicated vs hosted? we are evaluating both. security wants VPC and KMS. cost-wise we want to compare hosted per-token vs reserved capacity for predictable throughput

02:28 Jamie Lin: yeah, standard approach is baseline hosted to validate quality and latency, then Dedicated or Private if cost or data residency pushes it. for POC we can run a dedicated-reserved mimic using our dedicated pool or dedicated-like test bench
03:00 Liam O'Connor: timeline wise we have a board milestone end of April, so ideally POC results by mid-April. can that be done?

03:12 Carlos Vega: 6 weeks is doable: week 1 intake and data, week 2 synthetic/bench harness, weeks 3-4 run benchmarks and iterations, week 5 tuning and cost modelling, week 6 final report and handoff

03:30 Maya Patel: success criteria 
 1) p95 latency <200ms for median payloads, 2) cost per 1k requests under X (we need a target) 3) model accuracy/quality parity relative to our baseline (human eval on 200 prompts)
03:50 Jamie Lin: makes sense. for cost target can you give us ballpark or do you want us to propose?
03:58 Sophie Zhang: we want Redwood to propose cost and show dedicated vs hosted delta. security will need SOC2 docs and KMS integration details
04:10 Carlos Vega: noted. we'll include SOC2 and encryption docs. for KMS we support cloud KMS and customer-managed keys in Private deployments

04:27 Maya Patel: on QPS modeling 
 our peak sustained is around 30 qps, but with microsurges to 120 qps. most sessions are 1-2 requests per minute, so burstiness is important. also prefix caching is effective because many queries share context
04:50 Carlos Vega: prefix/KV cache will significantly lower cost for repeated context. we'll instrument cache hit rates in the benchmark and run scenarios with 0%, 30%, and 70% cache hit rates
05:10 Liam O'Connor: good call. also latency SLO needs to account for network egress between our VPC and Redwood's dedicated region. we prefer region us-west-2

05:30 Jamie Lin: we'll set test servers in us-west-2. for the bench harness we'll emulate the customer's network latency distribution, please share IP ranges if you want us to route test traffic through your infra
06:00 Maya Patel: we'll share anonymized traces. note some proper nouns might be scrubbed. hope that's fine for realistic modeling
06:15 Carlos Vega: totally fine, anonymized traces are ideal. we'll use them to derive QPS, token histograms, concurrency distributions and then run load tests that match shape

06:35 Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk) 
 and we should also discuss error budgets and fallback policies; if a dedicated node is saturated we fallback to hosted smaller model
06:55 Jamie Lin: yep fallback policy is part of the production design, for POC we'll simulate fallback and measure quality degradation

07:20 Sophia Zhang: about benchmarks 
 what exact metrics will you report?

07:28 Carlos Vega: we'll report p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k requests, CPU/GPU utilization, and end-to-end client observed latency including network. also quality metrics from the eval set
07:50 Maya Patel: ok. for model selection we currently use an open LLM that we've fine-tuned. will we be able to bring our fine-tuned weights to Redwood?

08:03 Jamie Lin: yes, Private and Dedicated allow customer weights; for hosted we can stage a model variant. we'll need to check model format 
 safetensors or pt 
 and size for kernel support

08:25 Liam O'Connor: any limitations on sequence length? some queries include long transcripts 
 up to 4k tokens occasionally
08:36 Carlos Vega: our runtime supports long context but perf drops as seq length increases; that's why we'll test 64/512/2048/4096 token buckets in the bench harness

09:00 Maya Patel: about observability 
 we want per-route cost and token-level breakdowns, can Redwood provide that in the console?
09:08 Jamie Lin: yes the Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency and token churn. we'll include example screenshots in the deliverable

09:30 Sophia Zhang: legal/procurement 
 what info do you need?
09:36 Jamie Lin: we'll send standard SOW draft and a security pack. procurement typically reviews SLA, data residency, and indemnity. we can start a redline once you have the SOW

10:00 Maya Patel: fine. one question 
 for the bench load pattern, should we model user think-time as poisson or fixed intervals? we've seen better match using poisson for our web chat
10:12 Carlos Vega: poisson or bursty closed-loop generators both ok; we'll mirror your observed inter-arrival distribution from traces. if you send traces we'll recreate the same pattern
10:30 Liam O'Connor: ok timeline recap?

10:33 Jamie Lin: recap 
 Redwood: share test plan + pricing by 3/14; Saffron: send anonymized traces + token histograms by 3/16; schedule VPC deep-dive week of 3/21; POC run mid-late March, final report mid-April
10:56 Sophia Zhang: cool. anything else on success criteria?

11:02 Maya Patel: also include a qualitative check 
 human eval for a 200-sample set and an automated regression metric. if quality drops more than 5% vs baseline we consider that a fail
11:20 Carlos Vega: noted. we'll include both automated BLEU/ROUGE style metrics and human eval notes
11:40 Jamie Lin: great. i'll follow up with the deck and benchmark template. thanks everyone
11:47 Sophia Zhang: thanks, bye
11:50 (recording stopped)
